channel.title: Financial Regulation Hub · IFSC
channel.description: New and amended rules from International Financial Services Centres Authority (GIFT City), as covered by the Financial Regulation Hub.

item.title: IFSC: Critical issues to be discussed at meetings of public interest directors
item.description:
IFSC · Circular · IFSCA/CMD/MIIT/PID/2026/001

Effective 2026-11-27.

Who it covers: Stock exchanges, clearing corporations and depositories in the IFSC.

  • Sets out the issues that public interest directors of market infrastructure institutions must discuss at their separate six-monthly meetings.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Market makers get up to two more working days to deliver in specified products
item.description:
IFSC · Circular

Effective 2026-11-25.

Who it covers: IFSC stock exchanges, clearing corporations and market makers.

  • The Master Circular for exchanges and clearing corporations is amended: market makers in specified products may deliver within up to two additional working days.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: All IFSC entities to act on CERT-In advisories and vulnerability notes
item.description:
IFSC · Circular · IFSCA circular dated 25-11-2026

Effective 2026-11-25.

Who it covers: All regulated entities, including systems run for them by the parent or third parties.

  • Comply with CERT-In advisories and vulnerability notes, including for systems run by the parent or vendors.
  • Set up a tracking mechanism within 30 days; assessment and patching duties apply to advisories issued from 25-11-2026.
  • Reminds entities that CERT-In's own directions (6-hour incident reporting, 180-day logs) apply independently.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Commodity trading notified as a financial service, and commodity trading contracts as a financial product
item.description:
IFSC · Notification · S.O. 6195(E) and S.O. 6196(E)

Effective 2026-11-13.

Who it covers: Entities wishing to set up commodity trading operations in the IFSC.

  • The Central Government notified "commodity trading" as a financial service and "commodity trading contract" as a financial product under section 3 of the IFSCA Act, 2019.
  • This lets IFSCA frame rules for commodity trading entities in the IFSC.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Registration of IFSC insurance offices stays valid on payment of the annual fee
item.description:
IFSC · Circular

Effective 2026-11-12.

Who it covers: IFSC Insurance Offices.

  • The certificate of registration of an IFSC Insurance Office continues to be valid as long as the annual fee is paid; no periodic renewal is needed.
  • This aligns with the Insurance Act as amended in 2025.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Bullion exchange and clearing corporation: quarterly non-compliance report
item.description:
IFSC · Circular

Effective 2026-11-12.

Who it covers: The bullion exchange and bullion clearing corporation in the IFSC.

  • Prescribes the format for reporting non-compliance under regulation 31 of the Bullion Market Regulations, 2025.
  • The report is due within 45 days of each quarter end; a nil report must be filed.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Two consultations: Financial Solicitation Professionals and model portfolios by research entities
item.description:
IFSC · Consultation paper

Who it covers: Capital market intermediaries, fund managers, distributors and research entities in the IFSC.

  • IFSCA proposes disclosure-based guidelines for engaging Financial Solicitation Professionals, and drops the idea of separate Financial Advisers regulations.
  • A second paper proposes to let research entities offer model portfolios.
  • Comments on both are due by 30-11-2026.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Reporting norms for TechFin and ancillary service providers, global in-house centres and book-keeping firms
item.description:
IFSC · Circular

Effective 2026-11-04.

Who it covers: TechFin and ancillary service providers, Global In-House Centres, and book-keeping, accounting, taxation and financial crime compliance service providers.

  • Monthly and quarterly reports are due by the 10th of the following month.
  • Anti-money laundering reports are half-yearly; the annual report is due by 31 May and audited financial statements by 30 September.
  • Material changes are reported within 30 days.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: No tax deducted at source on dividends between IFSC aircraft-leasing units
item.description:
IFSC · Notification · S.O. 6016(E)

Who it covers: Aircraft-leasing units in the IFSC.

  • The Central Board of Direct Taxes notified that no tax is deducted at source on dividends paid by one IFSC aircraft-leasing unit to another, on a declaration in the prescribed form.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Leasing of GPUs and connected data-centre equipment notified as a financial product
item.description:
IFSC · Notification · IFSCA/GN/2026/017

Effective 2026-10-29.

Who it covers: Finance companies and lessors in the IFSC.

  • Operating leases, and hybrids of operating and financial leases, of graphics processing units and connected data-centre equipment are a financial product in the IFSC.
  • The notification is dated 22-10-2026 and was published in the Gazette on 29-10-2026; IFSCA listed it on 04-11-2026.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Deadline for FME certification courses extended to 31-12-2026
item.description:
IFSC · Circular · F. No. IFSCA-AIF/127/2026-Capital Markets/1

Effective 2026-09-29.

Who it covers: KMPs and specified employees of fund management entities.

  • KMPs and employees have until 31-12-2026 to complete the specified certification course (ICSI or ICAI).

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Fund management entities must keep a website or webpage from 01-12-2026
item.description:
IFSC · Circular · No. IFSCA-SOF/2/2026-Capital Markets

Effective 2026-12-01.

Who it covers: All FMEs.

  • Authorised and Non-Retail FMEs may use their own site or a page on the parent's site; Retail FMEs need their own site.
  • The site shows the FME's profile, registration number, address and schemes.
  • New FMEs comply before starting and send the URL within 30 days of registration.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: IFSCA market abuse regulations replace SEBI insider trading and PFUTP rules in the IFSC
item.description:
IFSC · Regulations · No. IFSCA/GN/2026/012

Effective 2026-09-05.

Who it covers: Listed entities, designated persons, intermediaries and investors on IFSC markets.

  • Ban on communicating or trading on material non-public information.
  • Designated persons disclose trades within 2 trading days once quarterly trades exceed USD 25,000.
  • Trading plans disclosed 120 days ahead.
  • SEBI PIT Regulations, 2015 and PFUTP Regulations, 2003 no longer apply in the IFSC.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Every IFSC entity must hold a valid SEZ Letter of Approval at all times
item.description:
IFSC · Circular · IFSCA circular dated 10-08-2026

Effective 2026-08-10.

Who it covers: All regulated entities.

  • Hold a valid SEZ Letter of Approval and the IFSCA registration at all times.
  • Apply for renewal at least 2 months before expiry.
  • Replaces the directions of 03-04-2025.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Internet banking deadline for IBUs extended to 30-09-2026; onboarding bar from 01-10-2026
item.description:
IFSC · Circular · F.No. IFSCA-FMPP0BR/5/2024-Banking/2

Effective 2026-07-31.

Who it covers: IBUs offering liability products.

  • One-time extension of the internet banking deadline to 30-09-2026.
  • From 01-10-2026, an IBU that has not complied stops onboarding new customers for that liability product.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Capital relief for factoring exposures covered by eligible credit protection
item.description:
IFSC · Framework · F.No. IFSCA-FCR0ITFS/2/2024-Banking

Effective 2026-07-21.

Who it covers: Factors and Banking Units with factoring exposures.

  • The protected portion takes the risk weight of the protection provider.
  • Eligible providers include sovereigns, export credit agencies, MDBs, banks, regulated financial institutions, IFSC insurance offices and import factors.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Internet banking for IBUs: deadline 31-07-2026 and clarifications
item.description:
IFSC · Circular · F.No. IFSCA-FMPP0BR/5/2024-Banking/1

Effective 2026-06-30.

Who it covers: IBUs offering liability products.

  • "All linked accounts" covers deposit and loan accounts.
  • Live rates on the dashboard are not mandatory.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: IFSCA (Managing General Agents) Regulations, 2026
item.description:
IFSC · Regulations · Notified 08-06-2026

Effective 2026-06-12.

Who it covers: Managing general agents acting from the IFSC for foreign insurers.

  • Foreign insurer net worth of at least USD 100 million.
  • MGA capital of USD 500,000 held with an IBU, net worth of USD 250,000 or 50% of capital, whichever is higher, and a lien-marked deposit of USD 10,000 plus 10% of the minimum capital.
  • Binding authority agreement, fiduciary premium accounts and referral of claims above USD 10,000 to the insurer.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Annual compliance audit report and certificate for CMIs by 30 September
item.description:
IFSC · Circular · IFSCA circular dated 05-06-2026

Effective 2026-06-05.

Who it covers: Capital market intermediaries.

  • Submit the annual compliance audit report and certificate by email by 30 September, starting with FY 2025-26.
  • Broker dealers, clearing members and depository participants also file with the market infrastructure institutions.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Regulated entities encouraged to publish a Consumer Charter
item.description:
IFSC · Circular · F. No. IFSCA-LPRA/4/2025

Effective 2026-05-08.

Who it covers: Regulated entities dealing with retail consumers.

  • Entities dealing with retail consumers are encouraged to publish a Consumer Charter.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Finance Company Regulations amended (May 2026)
item.description:
IFSC · Amendment Regulations · IFSCA/GN/2026/009

Effective 2026-05-07.

Who it covers: Finance Companies and Finance Units.

  • Defines a Special Purpose Vehicle: a finance company incorporated or administered by a Trust and Company Service Provider authorised under the TechFin and Ancillary Services Regulations, 2025.
  • Leasing or financing by an SPV is added as a permitted activity, with an owned fund requirement linked to the Companies Act minimum.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Scheme fiduciaries may not also provide administration, valuation, audit or loans to the scheme
item.description:
IFSC · Circular · F. No. IFSCA-IF-10PR/7/2024-Capital Markets

Effective 2026-04-10.

Who it covers: FMEs and the trustees, boards or designated partners of their schemes.

  • A fiduciary may not provide fund administration, valuation, audit or lending to the same scheme, directly or through an associate.
  • Existing schemes comply by 30-09-2026.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: New reporting norms for capital market intermediaries
item.description:
IFSC · Circular · F.No.1/IFSCA/CMI Supervision/2023-24

Effective 2026-04-08.

Who it covers: Capital market intermediaries.

  • Quarterly reports within 21 calendar days of quarter end.
  • Half-yearly AML compliance sheet.
  • Replaces the norms of 08-02-2024.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Certification course specified for FME KMPs and employees; KMP intimation process amended
item.description:
IFSC · Circular · IFSCA circulars dated 01-04-2026

Effective 2026-04-01.

Who it covers: Fund management entities and their KMPs and employees.

  • IFSCA specified a certification course (offered by ICSI; ICAI added on 10-08-2026).
  • The KMP circular of 20-02-2025 was amended to remove the 7-working-day comment period.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Three-year relief from parts of the cyber security guidelines for branches and small entities
item.description:
IFSC · Circular · IFSCA circular dated 10-03-2026

Effective 2026-03-10.

Who it covers: Branches of regulated entities, group-only entities such as global in-house centres, and entities with fewer than 10 employees.

  • Eligible entities adopt the parent's framework, with the parent CISO as designated officer.
  • They file a compliance certificate within 90 days of year end and still submit the annual audit.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: New IFSCA fee structure
item.description:
IFSC · Circular · IFSCA circular dated 02-03-2026

Effective 2026-03-02.

Who it covers: All applicants and regulated entities.

  • Application, registration, flat recurring and conditional recurring fees, with interest on delay.
  • Flat recurring fee due 1 April and payable by 30 April.
  • Replaces earlier fee circulars, including that of 08-04-2025.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: SWIFT naming, routing and broadcast requirements for IBUs
item.description:
IFSC · Circular · No. IFSCA-FMPP0BR/12/2025-Banking

Effective 2026-02-26.

Who it covers: IBUs using SWIFT.

  • BIC name to include "GIFT IFSC Banking Unit".
  • Routing rules for misdirected messages and a quarterly broadcast for one year.
  • Compliance report by 30-06-2026.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Unified registration for several capital market activities
item.description:
IFSC · Circular · No. IFSCA-PLNP/80/2024-Capital Markets

Effective 2026-02-16.

Who it covers: Applicants for more than one capital market activity.

  • One application through the Single Window IT System for several activities, with a fee for each.

Official source

item.title: IFSC: Finance companies serving outside clients must keep a website from 01-04-2026
item.description:
IFSC · Circular · No. IFSCA-FCR/4/2026-Banking

Effective 2026-04-01.

Who it covers: Finance Companies and Finance Units serving clients outside their group.

  • Show the certificate of registration, products, grievance procedure and KMP contacts.

Official source
